checks.claim: PROOF005 L:spatial-wick-measures, proof LF1194-1336: the positive spatial Wick measures converge weakly at arbitrary width rates; the limit measure is (4-alpha)k-homogeneous; it gives zero mass to the faces r_l=0 and l_i=T; the horizon-restricted integrals converge.
checks.reason: LF1195-1213: I recomputed the transform. gamma_b has Fourier multiplier exp(-b|xi|^2/2) against mu. The sum over edges e of xi_e.(x_j-x_h) equals the sum over l of eta_l.z_l. The Green transform is sin(r|eta|)/|eta|, and the damped Laplace transform at 1+lambda_l gives 1/((1+lambda_l)^2+|eta_l|^2). Fubini is justified by the finite Gaussian-weighted mu and the Green mass r. The integrand is nonnegative, so the transform increases as any width decreases. LF1216-1222: integrating exp(-s|xi|^2/2) against mu(B_r)=V r^alpha gives alpha V s^(-alpha/2) times the integral of u^(alpha-1)exp(-u^2/2), so the constant A is correct, with s=t+b>=t. LF1223-1246, Brownian occupation per fixed ordering: for the last remaining vertex, conditioning on the past gives (p_gap*gamma_b)(.)<=A*gap^(-alpha/2). Removing that vertex and its earlier partner leaves a Brownian law at the remaining times. Removal only enlarges gaps, so the selected gap is at least the original adjacent gap at a distinct right endpoint, and the negative exponent turns this into an upper bound. The Dirichlet integral with j parameters 1-alpha/2 and j parameters 1 gives Gamma(1-alpha/2)^j T^((2-alpha/2)j)/Gamma((2-alpha/2)j+1). The (2j)! orders cover all labelled time orders. LF1248-1288: reducing every width to eps_* increases the positive transform. The Green-to-heat identity holds because both Fourier transforms equal 1/(a^2+|xi|^2) (half of 2/(a^2+|xi|^2) on the heat side). Hence the factor 2^(-2k). The horizon insertion is correct (each half-line integral is 2, times 1/4 gives 1). Positivity extends the ordered domains to cubes. Spectral Cauchy-Schwarz gives A_12<=sqrt(S1 S2). The exponents v_i+w/2<=k give (1+S1)^k(1+S2)^k. With independent paths the constant is 2^(-2k-2)(int e^(-a/2)M_k)^2. The zero, white (alpha=d=1) and anisotropic cases use ball masses only. LF1290-1309: monotone, then dominated, convergence gives L_D(lambda) for every lambda>=0 and continuity at 0. On the compact cube [0,1]^(2k), integer moments plus Stone-Weierstrass give a unique cluster point. The continuous functions y^c with c>0 and the limit c->0 exclude mass at y_l=0 (r=infinity). The portmanteau inequality on closed neighbourhoods plus a cutoff handles bounded continuous test functions. Uniqueness of the limit for every width sequence gives convergence at arbitrary rates. LF1311-1314: letting lambda_l->infinity, dominated by the lambda=0 integrand, gives nu_D{r_l=0}=0. LF1316-1324: I rechecked G_(cr)(c dz)=c G_r(dz) (2k factors) and gamma_b(cx)=c^(-alpha)gamma_(b/c^2)(x) (k factors), together with 2k time Jacobians. The total is c^((4-alpha)k), and widths eps/c^2 still tend to 0, so the vague limit inherits homogeneity. LF1325-1334: dilates cA, c in [1,2], are disjoint, each has mass >=rho_D(A), and all lie in one compact set, which contradicts Radon finiteness. The empty-chain face is empty. The region {l_1<T_1, l_2<T_2} is bounded and its boundary is null for nu_D, so the bounded multiplier e^(sum r)phi passes to the limit. No defect found.

checks.claim: PROOF048 P:interval-coefficients, proof LF6476-6657: the uniform bound C^k R^k T^(beta k)/(k!)^nu holds for the 2k-th ordinary energy coefficient of the interval-field phase evolution, and the summed phase bound follows.
checks.reason: LF6477-6490: enlarging L to max{1,L} and replacing sigma by |sigma| with a sign flip of the independent field preserve the hypotheses and the law. Band projection contracts every X_rho norm. LF6492-6535, ordinary versus exponential coefficients: the U_r are plain power-series coefficients. The entire majorant uses a complex-coefficient Gaussian multiplication norm <= 2 sqrt(n+1) ||c|| with ||c||^2 <= z_*^2 v_max, the simplex volume T^n/n!, an insertion cost 1/lambda, and the free bound e^(lambda T/2). Cauchy on the polydisc of radius 2z_* gives coefficient bounds whose geometric product is 2^|F|, which justifies absolute convergence of the energy double series at a fixed family. LF6537-6565, parity and local cutoff: for real s, [s^(2k)] equals the sum over |r|+|q|=2k of Q_(r,q). Colour reflection multiplies U_r by (-1)^(r_i), so r_i+q_i must be even. There are at most k active colours and at most prod(2k_i+1) <= 3^k splits. Since r_i, q_i <= 2k_i = N_i, Lemma L:finite-word-cutoff keeps both selected coefficients exactly. LF6567-6609: Lemma L:fixed-split is applied with sigma^2 <= c h^(-alpha0). The table weights follow: R h^beta (1+1/(lambda h)) with one charge; R lambda^(alpha-2) h^(2-alpha0); R^l h^(beta l)(1+l/(lambda h))^2/(l!)^nu. Positive-power expansion before inverse lengths: h^(beta l) + (2l/lambda)h^(beta l-1) + (l^2/lambda^2)h^(beta l-2) has positive powers since beta>2 and l>=2, and the singleton powers beta, beta-1, 2-alpha0 are positive. So each whole weight increases with h, and evaluation at h=LT/i is legitimate. I recomputed the substitution with lambda=k/T: R lambda^(alpha-2)(LT/i)^(2-alpha0) = R L^(2-alpha0) k^(alpha-2) T^beta i^(-p), and 1+l i/(kL) <= 1+l i/k since L>=1. This reproduces v_i and b_(i,l) of Lemma L:inventory-product. Each singleton's three splits are <= 3(m_i+c_i), so 3^k is counted once. LF6611-6620: the sum over k-vectors of products of weights equals the z^k coefficient of the product of generating series, with empty colours w_(i,0)=1 and no multinomial factor. I spot-checked the inventory lemma: z=k^nu/4; the 1+Q separation with the log integral of order k^(1/p); i<=k via S_nu(4P_i) and beta/nu>1; i>k tails of order k^(alpha0) and k^(2alpha0-1); Cauchy gives theta^(-k) k^(-nu k) e^(Ck). LF6622-6656, global L^2 domination including empty words: mode and band limits identify the fixed words at fixed eps and family, and the nonuniform v_max is used only for identification. The zero-order energy is <= e||v||^2 (lambda=1/T), and odd coefficients vanish. The absolutely convergent series gives (e+Y-1) <= eY because Y>=1. No defect found.

minor: PROOF033 LF4350-4373, LF4679-4691: Chen-Hu Theorem 1.2 and (5.15) print the homogeneity (1.8) and the functional (1.11) in density notation. Applying them to a possibly singular tempered-measure endpoint Gamma_st relies on the source's generalized-covariance convention (F126 LF535-560) and on the non-target Lemma L:physical-spectral-energy for the measure form of M_st. The reading is consistent and the source covers generalized covariances, but the proof could say explicitly that (1.8) is read distributionally (measure scaling r^(3-chi)).

PROOF005 LF1306-1309: the step from 'every width sequence has the same limit' to joint convergence at arbitrary relative rates implicitly uses that the weak topology on uniformly bounded measures on the compact cube is metrizable. This is correct but unstated.

PROOF048 LF6509-6514: the entire majorant uses the multiplication bound for a complex-coefficient Gaussian combination (creation norm sqrt(n+1)||c|| with complex modulus). It holds, but the proof states the bound only for the real instantaneous field.
PROOF047 LF6204-6205: the count actually gives M <= 2|A|+m+1 <= 2k+1. The stated 3k+1 is valid but loose and only affects the explicit C_split, not correctness.

limitations: This is a bounded AI depth audit of five proof environments only. It is not human verification, a whole-paper verdict, a novelty audit, a compile or PDF visual check, or adoption or delivery credit. No full-project completion is stated or implied.
The 27 \input modules (F001 LF8037-8063) were not supplied and were not read. None is referenced by the five target proofs.

These are: Chen-Hu Theorem 3.8(i), (5.1) and (5.15); Chen 2023 Theorem 1.1; Crouzeix-Palencia Theorem 6 and display (3). F126 is a text extraction with partly garbled formulas; the (5.15) normalization at p=2 was read from that extraction.
Confidence is medium, not high. The reconstruction is a single adversarial pass, and some constant chains in supporting lemmas were spot-checked rather than fully re-derived.
